name: mailwarden
description: Gmail MCP server for inbox triage: re-verified search, labels, archive/trash, mailbox-side snooze, triage digest, RFC 8058 unsubscribe. No send tools by design.
long_description:
mailwarden is a native Gmail MCP server built for triage, not correspondence. It searches (and re-verifies every hit against the live labels — Gmail's index is unreliable for read-state operators), reads threads, moves mail between labels, archives, trashes and untrashes, snoozes on the mailbox side (a label plus a sweep — no local state, so the snooze survives a restart and shows in the Gmail UI), builds a triage digest, lists subscriptions by sender and unsubscribes via RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe.

By design there is no compose, reply, forward or send tool, and `create_filter` never produces a forwarding rule — so a prompt-injected mail has no exfiltration path through this server. Nothing is deleted permanently (trash/untrash only), and there is no mailbox mirror or cache: every call goes live to the Gmail API.

Setup is a one-time OAuth consent to YOUR OWN Google Cloud OAuth client — the refresh token stays in `~/.mailwarden/` on this machine. Run `npx -y mailwarden --auth` once (guide: https://github.com/csitte/mailwarden/blob/main/docs/SETUP.md), then this bundle finds the token. `npx -y mailwarden --check` diagnoses an incomplete setup.

tools.title: Tool tiers
tools.description: Comma-separated subset of read, manage, filters. Fewer tiers = fewer tools; set the same value when authorizing (`MAILWARDEN_TOOLS=read npx -y mailwarden --auth`) and the OAuth scope narrows with it (read alone is gmail.readonly, where Google itself enforces no-send). Must not exceed what you authorized.
